parameters.excerpt: Each atomic instruction has two bits, _aq_ and _rl_, used to specify additional memory ordering constraints as viewed by other RISC-V harts.
parameters.reasoning: The _aq_ and _rl_ bits are direct implementation choices that specify memory ordering constraints for atomic instructions.

parameters.excerpt: An implementation can register an arbitrarily large reservation set on each LR, provided the reservation set includes all bytes of the addressed data word or doubleword.
parameters.reasoning: The size of the reservation set for LR instructions is an implementation choice, allowing for flexibility in how many bytes can be reserved.

parameters.excerpt: The misaligned atomicity granule PMA specifies the size of a misaligned atomicity granule, a power-of-two number of bytes.
parameters.reasoning: The size of the misaligned atomicity granule is an implementation-defined parameter that can vary, allowing for different implementations to support different sizes.

parameters.excerpt: If the _aq_ bit is set, then no later memory operations in this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place before the AMO.
parameters.reasoning: The choice to set the _aq_ bit for AMO operations is a direct implementation decision that affects memory operation visibility.

parameters.excerpt: If the _rl_ bit is set, then other RISC-V harts will not observe the AMO before memory accesses preceding the AMO in this RISC-V hart.
parameters.reasoning: The implementation can choose whether to set the _rl_ bit for AMO operations, which affects the visibility of memory operations across harts.
